title: through the viewfinder
author: immorality
summary: Mydei regards him thoughtfully, "…I saw Dawn. It was the film that drew me to this university." His heart races as he croaks out, "Really?" "Yes," he pauses as if trying to find the right words to say, "People get hung up on the technical marvel of it, but I think at its core it's about someone who is a victim of their circumstances, weighed down by everyone's expectations and his own, but you've already heard enough of other peoples' thoughts on your film, haven't you?" "I haven't heard enough of yours," he says softly. As a teaching assistant for one of the least sought after electives, Phainon ends up having to partner up with one of his students, Mydei—a quiet yet warm-hearted man who seems far divorced from the image of a film major—while also having to juggle his film thesis and creative burnout in order to graduate. Together they find out there’s more than meets the eye as they direct each other’s films.

FADE IN:

Work Text:

INT. MEDIA CLASSROOM 3. MIDDAY.
1

A medium wide shot of PROFESSOR CICERO, a gray-haired man in his mid-forties, with a stern look on his face as he paces back and forth whilst holding a syllabus.

“I know this class is an elective, but I still expect you all to take it just as seriously as a mandatory class,” Professor Cicero says, “I have had students fail prior because they underestimated the amount of time needed to be dedicated to coursework or racked up too many absences with the idea that this class is lax on attendance. Every deadline for this semester is outlined within the syllabus, please make sure to make note of them—I do not accept late work under any circumstances. If the requirements are too strenuous alongside your other coursework, you are free to drop the class within the next two weeks, otherwise it will be marked as a withdrawal permanently on your academic records. If you have any questions, please feel free to ask me or the TA. Now, if you would introduce yourself, Phainon.”

The aforementioned man waves, his smile like sunlight, “Hello, I’m Phainon, the teaching assistant for this semester. I have office hours every Sunday afternoon, Tuesday evening, and Thursday night. Please do not hesitate to contact me if any issues arise or if you need any guidance with the coursework.”

Cicero starts, excitement fueling his blabbering, “Yes, please make good use of Phainon, he has been one of the best pupils I have ever had the luxury of teaching. His short film, Dawn was shown at the Chrysos Festival, the largest independent cinema festival in all of Amphoreus. He also has an internship at Studio Era—”

“You flatter me so Professor,” Phainon interjects with a curt laugh, “but that is enough about me. Shall we go over the syllabus?”

“Right, of course.”

Phainon continues, “In this course Media and Medium: A Look Through the Lens, there are two major assignments with one final project. The two assignments and final will consist of short films that you all will create—there are no limitations in place for these films. You can use CGI, make a stop motion animation, use your phone to shoot—the sky is the limit.”

“In addition to your projects,” Professor Cicero interjects, “every other week Phainon will be screening a film during the night time block for this course. You will be required to write a one-to-two page analysis on the films he shows. During the weeks where there isn't a screening, Phainon has graciously volunteered to host optional work sessions in the media lab.”

“The first screening will be this Wednesday night. They are just as mandatory as the lectures and I will be taking attendance in Professor Cicero’s stead.”

“Any questions?” the professor asks.

The room is silent—excluding a few awkward, painfully dry coughs.

“Good, you are all dismissed.”

Phainon stands up and projects over all of the hasty shuffling, “Remember the first screening is this Wednesday night. I hope to see you all there.”

As the students file out, Phainon’s eyes land on someone he can only describe as breathtaking.

The man slowly packs his leather messenger bag and slips on his headphones laden in matte stickers, mussing up his strawberry blonde hair; his pretty, pink lips set in a frown. He doesn’t look like the type to enjoy films—Phainon halts that train of thought, he shouldn't be assumptive. They make brief eye contact and Phainon's pulse quickens in response; his eyes are like a wildfire, all-consuming and intense.

He feels a tap on his shoulder, splintering his focus, when he looks back—the man is gone.

“Ah, Phainon, before you leave, could you make sure to go over the documents on my desk?” Professor Cicero asks.

He hopes the disappointment isn't clear on his face as he gives Cicero his divided attention, “Of course, right away, Professor.”

CUT TO:

Work Text:

INT. MEDIA CLASSROOM 3. NIGHT.
2

Phainon tinkers with the projector while he waits for his students to file in for the screening. His attention is drawn away from his task as the first student arrives ten minutes early.

He instantly recognizes the stoic man from the first day of class.

Phainon quickly finds himself stumbling over his assumptions once more. Punctuality is a hard thing to ask of university students and it is even rarer for classes that aren't necessarily required—least of all did he expect it from a man that dresses like a delinquent and whose default emotion is unenthused. His mother taught him to not judge books by their covers; he should set aside his biases for a moment.

Recalling his manners, Phainon calls out from the projection booth door after a long stretch of silence, “Welcome in.”

“Thanks,” he replies, gruffly.

His voice isn't what he expected at all, but he finds that it isn't unpleasant to the ear—not in the slightest.

Phainon watches him with growing interest as he procures a small notepad and a pen from his bag; tapping the pen quietly against the paper to occupy himself, his face creased with boredom.

“Do you always arrive to classes early?” Phainon asks in an attempt at small talk.

“No.”

“Oh,” he says, a bit caught off guard by his curt response, but he's not one to be easily deterred, “is there a particular reason you did today?”

His pen tapping stops abruptly as he lets out a soft sigh, “My dorm is nearby.”

“Really? So is mine. Are you in the Genesis building?”

He gives a slight nod, still not very receptive to Phainon’s effort to make conversation.

The door opens as a few more students arrive and Phainon swears he can see the relief on the other man’s face. If it wasn't before, he's sure his ego is a bit bruised from the interaction. He walks back over to the projector, deflated like a balloon, and finishes setting up the film for viewing.

After the rest of the students file in, Phainon leaves the booth and places a sign-in sheet on one of the tables located near the exit.

“Everyone please make sure to sign your name before the end of today's screening. I’ll do one more reminder before I dismiss you all tonight. I have seen people forget to sign-in despite attending every screening and it's always a headache to sort out previously marked absences in the system, so let's avoid letting it come to that if we can.”

He gets a few exasperated ‘okay’s in response.

Phainon continues, “Tonight we will be watching an experimental film by Mr. Reca, called A Fading Nebula. It is his most popular work to date and probably a movie you have seen before if you have even the slightest bit of interest in films. Make sure to take notes as you all will have a short essay due on this work next week.”

“Phainon,” a student interjects, “will these films be available outside of screenings?”

“Good question. Yes, every film I show for the screenings will be available to watch at home. On the site where you turn in your assignments, I have a section by the PDF for the syllabus with the links for each film and a password that you can enter to access it on Filmeo. I will be updating it every other week, so in case you were wondering, you will not be able to watch all of the films in advance.”

A few disgruntled groans fill the air.

“I know, I know,” he chuckles, “but it is what Professor Cicero prefers I do. But, I’ll let you all in on a little secret—if you attend my office hours, I wouldn't mind divulging which films we are going to watch in the near future. Now if you all would like, you may all leave your items at the tables and sit in the cinema seats.”

Phainon enters the booth once more as he hears the squeaks of the chairs die down below, presses play on the DVD player nestled at the bottom of the media cart, and slumps in the padded chair by the projector. He's seen this film many times prior and as gripping as it is, he finds sleep softly tugging him under before he's even cognizant of it.

He jolts awake, drool plastered to his cheek, as he feels a firm hand on his shoulder. The rest of the dim room lies empty before him as his eyes regain their focus. Mortification floods in—falling asleep is already terrible enough, but on the first day of supervising the class is irresponsible. He rubs his hand against his face in shame, cringing away as he feels the saliva cling to his palm.

“The film ended thirty minutes ago, but you seemed so tired I didn't want to disturb you,” the man with a voice like rich honey says.

“I’m sorry to make you stay after,” Phainon replies, genuinely remorseful.

“Don't be,” he shrugs, “but you should leave soon. Security just came around to lock the door and I said you needed a little more time.”

His mouth opens slightly in soft surprise from his thoughtfulness before he responds, “Thanks.”

“Here,” he holds out the attendance sheet, “I made sure everyone signed it.”

“I think you're more suited to be the TA than I am,” Phainon chuckles.

“Maybe,” he says dryly.

A joke, Phainon realizes rather belatedly, his delivery was so impassive he almost took it as a statement.

Before he can reply back, the man is already at the threshold of the booth. He slides on his headphones and is out the door with a small courtesy nod after quickly packing his things. His haste, Phainon thinks, is because he doesn't want to inconvenience the security guards, so he follows suit. He locks the projection booth behind him and exits the screening room with a sigh.

He should follow his mother's teachings more closely.

Books don't always fit their covers.

CUT TO:

Work Text:

INT. MEDIA CLASSROOM 3. MIDDAY - TWO WEEKS LATER
3

Phainon hands out papers detailing an upcoming project while Professor Cicero speaks from his podium—a small manual projector screen lies behind him showing the guidelines and expectations for his students’ first films.

“Thank you to everyone who has decided to keep this elective. The number of students has dwindled greatly, but I think it will allow us to spend more time on thoughtful critique and for everyone's films to receive the amount of attention they deserve.”

Professor Cicero points to the screen as he continues, “Your first major assignment will be a duo project on the topic of beauty—you may interpret the word as you like, but you will not be shooting your own film, instead you will direct your assigned partner to create your vision. This project will be an exercise in your ability to give direction, organize your ideas, and give you a bit of insight on how your partner may interpret your work.”

One student raises their hand, “Will we be able to choose our partners?”

“No, I will be pairing you all off.”

Phainon tunes out Professor Cicero’s voice as he works on revising the third draft of his thesis film’s screenplay. His advisor has been mercilessly picking apart every aspect of it and while he does agree it is a bit uninspired compared to his usual work, the pressure to make it perfect is starting to take a toll on him. The last time he got even a fraction of decent sleep was when he conked out during the screening two weeks ago. His search history is filled with varying queries of ‘how much sleep deprivation is safe without dying’ because of how many all-nighters he’s been pulling. He hopes that this draft will be the last so that he can begin searching for crew members and start wrapping up pre-production. At the pace he's moving, he's worried if he'll even gradu—

“Ah, it seems we don't have enough pairs. Phainon would you be Mydei’s partner?”

Phainon’s heart nearly stops.

He was pleasantly surprised and secretly a little thankful that Mydeimos didn't drop this course when he saw his name in the system while tallying the attendance today in Professor Cicero's stead and it's not just because of his looks, which plays a small part, he finds himself intrigued by his writing. Mydei's essay from the week prior was the best of the bunch, even Phainon who isn't particularly fond of the writing portion that accompanies film theory couldn't put it down. He's just as blunt on paper, but his conciseness is a breath of fresh air compared to the other students trying to meet the minimum word count. He also understands the work at its core and presents a perspective on the themes that Phainon hadn't even considered, for how much he's seen A Fading Nebula, Mydei's piece taught him something new.

“Oh, sure,” he replies, hoping that his voice isn’t betraying him.

“Great, I hope this won’t be too much of a burden on you as I know you’re also working on your thesis,” Cicero says.

It is a bit of an inconvenience if he’s being honest, but getting to work with his—well, he’s not quite sure what Mydei is to him yet, crush seems too strong of a word when he barely knows him, but he is interested in getting to know him—to be his eyes for his film.

He wonders what Mydei thinks of the word 'beauty'.

He smiles, “Not at all.”

FADE IN:

Work Text:

INT. MEDIA LAB. NIGHT.
4

Wide shot of the dimly-lit media lab as Phainon and Mydei sit in front of two iMac computers as they converse about the upcoming project. Some students are quietly working at their computers on either side of them or are occupied with other coursework at the tables lined up in the center of the room; while others chatter away loudly with no regard for the implied rule of silence, earning themselves a few annoyed hushes.

“This will be the only group project, I promise,” Phainon jests.

“I know. I read the syllabus,” he replies rather seriously.

“Right,” he says. Trying to stave off the awkward atmosphere, he adds, “do you have an idea yet for what you would like to do?”

Mydei reaches into his bag and pulls out a well-worn leather-bound notebook covered in stickers with an assortment of eclectic sticky notes jutting out the sides, “I made a general outline and a rough shot list.”

“Wow, you’re more prepared than I am.”

“I wouldn’t expect you to take it too seriously, you’re the TA after all.”

“I take everything seriously,” he says, mildly offended.

Mydei gives him a weird look before handing him his notebook. There is another thing he’s noticed about him prior and it’s that he is oddly meticulous, even his ‘rough’ notes are carefully crafted and thoroughly explained. Despite his earlier words, guilt starts to gnaw at him for not taking this as seriously as Mydei is.

"It's okay," Mydei says.

Phainon looks up from the notebook, perplexed, "What?"

"I said, it's okay—you had this worried look on your face. I don't care if you haven't come up with a draft for your film yet."

"Are you trying to cheer me up?" he laughs.

Mydei's stoic mask doesn't slip one bit, "No. It was just weird seeing you like that."

His heart thumps at his admission, "You don't think seriousness befits me?"

"Not in the slightest."

"How harsh."

One of the other students from their class walks up to their station, "Oh, hey, Phainon, I know it's not your office hours, but do you think you could help me with something?"

He turns to Mydei to gauge his reaction, semi-hoping that he'll say they're busy, but it's a futile dream—Mydei just shrugs in response. He turns back to the student, slightly defeated, "Sure, what do you need help with?"

He follows them across the lab to where they're situated in a corner with their project partner, a small laptop shared between them.

"In your film Dawn you had this shot, but I can't figure it out. Was it done in post?"

On their computer screen is a sequence he edited together where the protagonist of his film lies on the ground as gold trickles from his wounds; the shot is slowly revealed by a drop of ink dispersing in water.

He points to the timeline they have open in Before Effects, "Here I had one layer with the ink spill and the main footage underneath had the track matte set to luma inverted matte. The layer order in the timeline matters."

"Thank you so much. We've been arguing over how you might have accomplished it for the past half-hour."

"I'm glad to have settled the debate for you both."

The other student pipes up, "I can't wait to see what you come up with for your thesis. I hope I can make it to the screening."

If there will even be one at this rate, he thinks bitterly.

He musters a smile, "I hope it won't disappoint."

"I doubt it, you're like a prodigy."

The urge to frown almost becomes impossible to stave off.

"Not at all," he laughs, "well, I guess I will see you both next week."

He sighs when he's out of earshot. It's already hard enough trying to work on the piece that will determine whether he graduates or not, it's even worse when he's trying to shoulder the weight of everyone's expectations while fighting imposter syndrome. Dawn's success was a fluke, a movie born from the depths of his heart—an amateur's shallow attempt at being profound; despite all of the praise for it, the opportunities, it feels like no one truly understands what he was trying to convey.

"Are you okay?" Mydei asks when he sits back down.

He passes Mydei his notebook that he didn't realize was still clenched in one hand with a small smile, "I'm fine. Just a little tired."

"Then should we just meet up another time then?"

"No," Phainon says a little too quickly, earning a slightly confused look from Mydei, "we can continue."

"If you insist."

"I didn't get to say it earlier, but your rough notes are nice and easy to follow."

"Thanks."

After a beat of comfortable silence, a question that's been on his mind slips out, "Pardon my curiosity, but what made you decide to pursue film?"

Mydei looks at him for a long moment, one that stretches on for so long he nearly wonders if he poked a hornet's nest, but he eventually says, "What I can't convey through words, I can through film. Nothing more, nothing less."

"Not because you enjoy it?"

"My enjoyment is secondary."

"It seems you use it to vent too."

Mydei regards him thoughtfully, "…I saw Dawn. It was the film that drew me to this university."

His heart races as he croaks out, "Really?"

"Yes," he pauses as if trying to find the right words to say, "People get hung up on the technical marvel of it, but I think at its core it's about someone who is a victim of their circumstances, weighed down by everyone's expectations and his own, but you've already heard enough of other peoples' thoughts on your film, haven't you?"

"I haven't heard enough of yours," he says softly.

Mydei's cheeks fill with color, a delicate pink in the dim light, "You won't coax any more out of me."

"How unfortunate," Phainon teases, then he says a bit more earnestly, "for what it's worth, I think you're very good with words."

He receives a glare that is more endearing than fearsome in response.

CUT TO:

Work Text:

EXT. CAMPUS COURTYARD. DAY.
5

Medium wide shot of Phainon wiping the sweat from his forehead as Mydei adjusts a Sony FX30 that rests on top of a tall, black tripod. The COURTYARD is filled with students enjoying their lunches on the freshly-cut green grass while others briskly walk by on their way to their classes, their voices carrying on the wind as they converse.

Phainon’s heart flutters pathetically as he watches Mydei deep in concentration, his brow furrowed as he tries to mount the camera properly—he wonders if Mydei has considered acting before, he certainly has the face for it. Mydei softly grunts under his breath as the camera sits lopsidedly on the quick-release plate—another failed attempt, after a few more moments of watching him struggle, Phainon takes pity on him and mounts the camera with ease.

“Don't sweat not being able to get it on easily. I've been trying to convince the media rental center that these tripods suck. More people have broken them and the cameras than I can count on one hand," Phainon assures him.

“A moment longer and I would have figured it out," he huffs, almost petulant.

"I'm sure you would have," Phainon says, though he realizes belatedly how sardonic it sounds when Mydei's frown deepens.

"Sorry—"

Mydei sighs as he picks up Phainon's shot list to jog his memory, "It's fine. Would you rather shoot first or me?"

"You can go on ahead, I'll get out of your way."

This project has been the least of his worries and unfortunately that has extended to his uninspired shot list. He's never been a coaster in his life, always the overachiever, but that pull that inspires him to create has begun to fizzle out like a defective firecracker.

Mydei aims the camera at the red cedar tree planted in the center of the courtyard; he watches as Mydei's fingers adjust the focus ring and his eyes check the image projected on the monitor. When he has the shot lined up, he calls Phainon over to approve it before he starts rolling.

It's exactly as he had pictured it and somehow that bothers him.

Itching to know about Mydei's opinion, he asks, "What would you change about this shot?"

"Everything. It's pretty, yes, but I feel like it lacks intention."

He starts, "Then—"

"Sit."

Phainon quickly does as he's told and rests on one of the benches in front of the tree. Mydei angles the camera down and adjusts the focus once more before he starts recording. Heat creeps up his cheeks as he looks away from the lens—he feels exposed, like Mydei's eyes are piercing through him from where they're trained on the monitor. He wonders if he knows how hard his heart is beating right now, if the blush that coats his cheeks gives him away. If it does, Mydei stays silent, holding his budding affection like a secret.

Mydei ushers him over wordlessly, the space between them nearly nonexistent as he crowds him to look at the monitor.

It's a rather intimate close up.

Under normal circumstances looking straight at the camera renders the footage unusable, but Mydei frames it purposefully as if he's caught his lover mid glance—something that he allows the viewer to be privy to. In contrast, the scene he asked Mydei to capture pales greatly in comparison, a pretty shot devoid of meaning.

"Your shot list seems like it's been stripped of all personality. Why is that?" Mydei asks.

"I don't think my work for this project matters much in the grand scheme of things."

"I didn't think Okhema's golden boy would take shortcuts."

His statement stings, it makes bitterness come easy and settle heavy on his tongue, "And you're oddly serious about work for an elective."

Mydei scoffs, "I don't have a choice. If I fail any class, I can give up my dream of pursuing film."

"Your parents aren't fond of the idea of trying to make a living out of art?"

"My mother gave me her blessing, my father on the other hand…" his expression sours, "sorry."

Remorse washes over him like a tidal wave, "There is no need to apologize, Mydei, I asked, you answered."

"…What about you?" he murmurs quietly.

"Me? You mean my parents?"

Mydei nods.

"Supportive, almost suffocatingly so sometimes."

"And you feel like you have to measure up to the hope that they place in you," Mydei says.

"Always."

"Despite my earlier words, I'd say you're allowed to slack off every once in a while."

He laughs softly, "I'd feel terrible if I did when you're trying so hard."

"I guess you'll just have to try and best me."

His laughter builds until it bubbles over like seafoam, "How can we make filming a competition?"

"Have you forgotten it's graded?"

"Art is subjective."

Mydei huffs as he folds his arms, "Until it's not."

"Are you pouting?"

"No."

"Fine, fine," he relents jokingly, "I'll compete with you."

"You're insufferable."

Phainon smiles, "I try."

When they finish wrapping up filming for the day, the sun is cradled deep in the horizon—the once lively courtyard is now quiet, lit by the dim, flickering streetlamps, the soft sound of footsteps filling the silence as few students walk to their night classes. Phainon watches as Mydei starts to disassemble the camera rig to fit it back into its pouch and before he gets very far, he musters up the courage to ask for Mydei to stay for a while in order to shoot some additional footage.

He tilts his head in question, his fingers pressed against the rim of the lens, “Why?”

“I need some B-roll for a different class,” Phainon lies.

Mydei eyes him skeptically, but relents, “Sure. What do you need me to do?”

Phainon didn't think he would get this far—he was so sure Mydei would decline. He has Mydei stand next to one of the streetlamps as he quickly reassembles the camera rig, his hands trembling slightly from nerves.

"Are you sure you won't need a tripod or a stabilizer?" Mydei teases.

"My hands are perfectly capable of recording right now."

He laughs, "If you insist."

Phainon lifts up the camera and fiddles with the settings until the exposure is just right, Mydei's features clear under the veil of the streetlight. Mydei tilts his head up. Phainon knows his gaze is bordering on carnal as he watches the bob of his Adam's apple, thoughts that he shouldn't have right now taunting him as he clears his throat. Mydei looks over at him, his eyes glinting in the cool fluorescent light and Phainon knows he's caught by the way he smirks at the lens.

CUT TO:

Work Text:

INT. GENESIS ROOM 33 - PHAINON’S ROOM. NIGHT.
6

Phainon sits on his bed looking at the timeline of his editing program of choice, Before Effects, with the footage he shot of Mydei staring back at him from the Project tab. The clock reads 03:00, his eyes half-lidded as his focus begins to leave him.

The last thing he should be doing right now is working on something other than his thesis, but he feels that inexplicable urge to create once more, the urge that has eluded him for so long—he knows that if he lets it slip through his fingers now, he'll spend forever chasing after it again. He drags the first clip onto his timeline, a close up shot of Mydei's face—the hardened lines of his cheek bones, the downward curve of his nose, and his long, soft eyelashes illuminated by the cool glow of the streetlamp. Then the next, an extreme close up of his eyes. Phainon could look into his eyes for hours, they're like a beautiful sunset or the last embers of a fervent flame. His tiredness begins to ebb the more he edits, the sun slowly illuminating his room until he remembers to glance at his clock again.

He figures since he's not going to get any rest that he should work on revising his proposal for the thirtieth time, but this time when he does, the words flow easily, his ideas flow freely, and that stubborn mental block melts away. When he emails the document to his advisor, he knows for a fact that she won't turn down this proposal.

CUT TO:

Work Text:

INT. FACULTY OFFICE 2. AFTERNOON.
7

AGLAEA lifts her head from her task with a small smile—eager to welcome Phainon into her office. Her expression falters slightly when she sees the dark circles under his eyes.

“Phainon, please tell me you haven't been neglecting your sleep schedule for coursework again,” his advisor says.

“If I told you I didn't, that would be a lie, Professor Aglaea.”

She sighs, “Have a seat.”

Awkwardly, he settles down on the chair across from her that is a tad too short for his legs and stretches them out until the tips of his sneakers disappear under her oak desk.

"Have you seen my newest proposal?" he says after a beat.

"Yes, it's quite a departure from your usual work, but I think that could be a good thing. If I may ask, did anything change between now and the last time we spoke?"

"Inspiration struck me."

"That it did," she agrees softly, "how are you faring with your classes?"

"They're fine. I think I'm doing more work with the class I am a TA for than my other two courses."

"Should I speak with Professor Cicero?"

"There's no need. I don't mind it. If anything it's giving me a bit of a fresh perspective on my own film."

"I'm glad to hear it."

"If I may ask, how have you been, Professor Aglaea?"

A frown sets on her lips, but it's quickly replaced with a tired smile, "I have been okay, thank you for your concern, Phainon."

"You and Doctor Anaxa are still not seeing eye-to-eye?"

"That man is more stubborn than an ox. I have spent more time in the Academic Records building these past two years than advising in order to rectify his overly harsh grades."

"I still appreciate you doing that for me too."

"Of course, someone has to keep him in check, but enough of that, have you picked a date for your screening?"

He deflates, "Not yet, I haven't even begun shooting."

"I'll put in a placeholder date for the time being."

"Thank you, and sorry for all of the trouble."

Glossary:
Chrysos Festival: Parody of the Cannes Film Festival, one of the most prestigious film festivals in the world.

CGI: Computer-generated imagery, not to be confused with AI generation.

Filmeo: A parody of Vimeo, a video and film hosting site.

Pre-production: The things you do before shooting a film: writing the script, organizing, finding crew members, etc.

Production: Shooting the actual film.

Post-production: Otherwise known as post, entails editing the film.

Shot list: A document that outlines how a scene is to be filmed, the shot size, the camera's location, etc.

Before Effects: Parody of After Effects

Track matte: In after effects, you can alter the transparency of layers by using either its alpha channel (what determines an image's transparency) or luminance (luma matte, brightness) to show another image through it. For example if you have a image with high black values, you can use luma inverted matte to show another image through the black pixels while leaving the white pixels untouched, for the opposite effect you would use luma matte.

Rolling: Recording

B-roll: Supplemental footage used interspersed with A-roll (the main footage), can be shots or visuals that complement dialogue (typically without audio of its own)

Rim light: Light on the edges of a subject, can be achieved with certain lighting techniques or in post if compositing with separated layers.

Rough Cut: A rough draft of a movie, the bare bones of putting all of the clips in a sequence without any editing.
